sanskrit_shloka:
अष्टावक्र उवाच ॥
न ते सङ्गोऽस्ति केनापि किं शुद्धस्त्यक्तुमिच्छसि ।
सङ्घातविलयं कुर्वन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥ ५-१॥
translation: Aṣṭāvakra said: You have attachment to no one and nothing; being pure, what do you wish to renounce? Dissolve the aggregates of body and mind, and thus enter absorption in the Self.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Aṣṭāvakra said: You have attachment to no one and nothing; being pure, what do you wish to renounce? Dissolve the aggregates of body and mind, and thus enter absorption in the Self.

commentary_faqs.question: What does Ashtavakra mean by 'dissolving the aggregates'?
commentary_faqs.answer: It refers to the process of de-identifying from the physical body, mental impressions, and sensory perceptions (the five koshas or aggregates) to realize the underlying pure Consciousness.

commentary_faqs.question: Why is the world compared to a bubble in the ocean?
commentary_faqs.answer: The metaphor illustrates that the world is a temporary manifestation that arises from, is supported by, and eventually dissolves back into the ocean of the Self, without ever being separate from it.

commentary_faqs.question: How does this chapter define equanimity?
commentary_faqs.answer: Equanimity is defined as remaining unchanged and stable (sama) regardless of external conditions like pleasure or pain, hope or despair, and even the ultimate duality of life and death.

sanskrit_shloka:
उदेति भवतो विश्वं वारिधेरिव बुद्बुदः ।
इति ज्ञात्वैकमात्मानमेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥ ५-२॥
translation: From you the universe arises, like a bubble from the ocean. Knowing the Self to be one, thus enter into absorption in That.

sanskrit_shloka:
प्रत्यक्षमप्यवस्तुत्वाद् विश्वं नास्त्यमले त्वयि ।
रज्जुसर्प इव व्यक्तमेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥ ५-३॥
translation: Though directly perceived, the world does not truly exist in you, the pure and stainless Self, just as the snake appearing in a rope is unreal. Thus enter into absorption.

sanskrit_shloka:
समदुःखसुखः पूर्ण आशानैराश्ययोः समः ।
समजीवितमृत्युः सन्नेवमेव लयं व्रज ॥ ५-४॥
translation: Equal in pain and pleasure, full in yourself, equal in hope and hopelessness, equal in life and death—being thus, enter into absorption in the Self.
